newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: GOLF-WESTWOOD WINS MALAYSIAN OPEN TO RECORD HAT-TRICK. [CORRECTED 22:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WESTWOOD WINS MALAYSIAN OPEN TO RECORD HAT-TRICK. [CORRECTED 22:43 GMT]

text.p: Britain's Lee Westwood snatched the $300,000 Malaysian Open championship on Sunday when he carded a final round three-under-par 69 for a final total of 274. It was his third tournament victory in succession (Corrects).
The 23-year old holed a birdie putt on the 18th green to finish 14-under-par for the tournament.

It gave him a two-stroke victory over American Larry Barber, who finished second on 276, while overnight leader Harumitsu Hamano of Japan finished equal fifth on 279 after a three-over-par final round of 75.
South African Retief Goosen came third, one stroke behind Barber, with a final round round of 65.

"Patience was the key today," said Westwood who had set the course record of 64 in the opening round and completed his third win in a row, having taken the Scandinavian Masters in Sweden and the Visa Taiheiyo championship.
